title: Brief content model (brief-model.yaml)
description: The single editorial artifact an agent authors for a stakeholder brief (SPEC 029, T-001). A deterministic projector (T-002) turns this into HTML; the agent never writes markup, digests or SHA-256 here — those are computed by the projector from the canonical source at projection time.

contract_version.description: Version of THIS schema/contract that the model was authored against (not a brief-shell/design axis — FR-010 unifies those elsewhere). Semantic version.

profile.description: Depth of coverage the agent commits to. Selects, together with domain, which routes exist (FR-005).

domain.description: Material domain of the initiative. Selects, together with profile, which routes exist (FR-005).

thesis.description: Brief thesis and global choices (plan.md §9.1, 'Brief thesis and global choices' table), carried once at the top of the model instead of once per agent per iteration.

decision_and_audience.description: The decision this brief exists to support, and who reads it to make it.

brief_thesis.description: The single sentence a reader must leave with.

repeated_component_treatment.description: Which source-defined collections need one record per item, and why (plan.md §9.1).

routes.description: The routes SELECTED for this profile×domain pair (FR-005). A route not selected is simply absent from this list — it does not need an N/A disposition (NG-002/EC-003).

relations.description: Material relationships (FR-004), declared as node/edge graphs. A block whose form is topology/sequence/risk-chain references one of these graphs via relation_ref instead of re-describing structure in prose.

routeId.description: Canonical route ids, exactly as enforced by scripts/validate_brief_candidate_inheritance.py:19. Note: the executive-brief-composition SKILL still says 'architecture.global' — that is contradiction A-02; this model uses the validator's vocabulary, 'architecture'.

executive_question.description: The executive question this route answers for its reader (plan.md §9.1 column 2). Optional: not every route needs a restated question beyond its blocks.

block.description: One route entry or one repeated-component record (e.g. one architecture zoom, one task dossier, one validation proof). Carries authored text, its provenance, and its declared visual form.

id.description: Stable id within the route, e.g. 'hero', 'T-001', 'zoom-ingestion', 'V-004'.

collection.description: Canonical id of the repeated source-defined collection this block belongs to, when it is a repeated component, e.g. 'execution.task', 'impact.surface', 'validation.proof' (plan.md §9.1).

text.description: Authored editorial content: narrative, hero copy, decision call, absence explanation, etc. Required for all coverage values except a bare not_applicable/discovery whose reason/discovery fields already carry the statement.

narrative_arc.description: Optional narrative arc label carried from plan.md §9.1 (e.g. 'delta → exposure → control → action').

form.description: Enumerated visual form (FR-006). The projector has its own implementation of each; 'prose' is always available as the escape hatch (R-002 mitigation).

form_reason.description: Why this form was chosen for this block. Required for every block, including 'prose' — 'prose' still needs a reason (e.g. 'projector has no implementation for this shape yet' or 'a single decided fact needs no diagram').

fields.description: Structured dossier fields as ordered label/value pairs (form: dossier, matrix, footprint, risk-chain). Real briefs use different field sets per domain (e.g. task dossiers: Resultado/Limite/Prova/Por-que-agora in one initiative, Escopo/Dependência/Risco-controle/Validação-evidência/Saída-agora in another) — the schema does not fix a fieldset, only the shape.

relation_ref.description: Id of an entry in the top-level relations[] this block renders (used with form topology/sequence/risk-chain).

source.description: Canonical relative path of the source this block is grounded in, e.g. 'spec.md', 'tasks.md', 'decision-log.md'. Even a not_applicable/discovery block cites the source that establishes the absence (plan.md §9.1: 'record a source-backed entry or an explicit N/A/discovery').

source_section.description: Heading locator inside the source, e.g. 'Functional requirements', '#T-001', 'D-004'.

fragment.description: Literal snippet that must occur verbatim in the source AND in the rendered block (FR-003). The agent copies it from the source; the projector computes and verifies its digest/SHA-256 — this model never carries a digest field. Required unless coverage is not_applicable (an absence has no positive fragment to lift).

absence.description: A source-backed disposition for a route/component that is not populated with positive content (plan.md §9.1: 'An inapplicable component requires a visible, source-backed absence card with reason and decision impact. A missing material fact becomes an owned discovery').

reason.description: Why this route/component genuinely does not apply, grounded in the cited source.

missing_fact.description: The specific fact the canonical sources do not provide.

decision_impact.description: What decision cannot be made, or is at risk, without this fact.

owner.description: Only when the source itself names an owner — never invented.

path.description: Only when the source itself names a resolution path — never invented.
